Summary: RivalCo this morning announced a bundled offer—discounted pricing for customers who adopt three or more of their modules; the workspace reactions show field teams alarmed about deal losses, analysts calling it an aggressive share-grab, and some customers saying the price is compelling but asking for clarity on integration/ROI.  
Likely objectives (speculative): force multi-product adoption to grow wallet share and lock customers into their ecosystem, accept short-term margin loss to win renewals/displace point competitors, and create urgency in procurement cycles.  
Option 1 — Match the bundle price company-wide: Pro—removes RivalCo’s immediate price advantage and protects at-risk deals; Con—compresses margins and risks escalating a price war.  
Option 2 — Targeted, value-based counteroffers (selective 3-product bundles for high-value segments, outcome guarantees, integration/service credits): Pro—preserves price discipline and emphasizes differentiation; Con—requires operational setup and will be slower to deploy.  
Option 3 — Hold and monitor + tactical sales plays (prioritize a competitor-win-risk account list, deploy battle cards, offer short-term account-level promotions/accelerators): Pro—low-cost and preserves long-term pricing; Con—may lose volume if RivalCo’s bundle proves widely irresistible—recommend preparing a 72-hour decision rubric and list of top 50 at-risk accounts for tomorrow’s meeting.
